e_solver_soundness_and_hull_completeness.note: 6/20 true discrete Pareto-frontier points are in the Lagrangian duality gap: individually non-dominated (no other single plan beats them on both axes) yet unreachable by ANY lambda for their own schedule, because different blocks have different sensitivities and their local rate-distortion curves don't share a common marginal-rate breakpoint. Textbook property of discrete/integer rate allocation (Everett / Shoham-Gersho), not a bug. Reported here, never gated.

exactness_refinement_trigger.rule: IF any G1 budget shows utilization < 97% (joint OR best-sequential), OR the final G1 margin lands within 0.15 points of the 0.4-point bar, THEN before finalizing G1 implement the exact per-schedule Pareto-set DP (multi-choice knapsack over the 12 blocks, dominance-pruned) for the joint arm AND for the sequential stages' bit allocation (fairness requires upgrading both arms together), and re-select plans.
exactness_refinement_trigger.fired: pre-emptively (89.0-95.2% at 4/6 budgets (old hull-based solver, old WA4-inclusive menu); menu restriction expected to widen gaps)
exactness_refinement_trigger.note: Post-upgrade utilization (Section 25b) is retained as a granularity diagnostic, not an optimality concern -- gate (e)'s DP-exactness assertion (Section 18) proves the exact DP reaches the true per-schedule optimum, including duality-gap points the lambda-sweep could not reach. G1-dependent fields added retrospectively in Section 27b.

pred_vs_measured_fidelity_all_plans_note: Corrected: excludes the 2 retained WA4 evidence rows (X8/X9, excluded_out_of_menu=True; see F-X1) from the pooled fit. The uncorrected/polluted fit (includes those rows) is recorded separately below for the record and is never the reported fidelity number.

F_X1_wa4_menu_enforcement.title: WA4 superlinear composition -> menu enforcement
F_X1_wa4_menu_enforcement.statement: The two WA4 Family-X configs (X8: WA4 on blocks {2,3,4} + merge(11,32); X9: WA4 on blocks {6,7} + merge(5,64)) measured ratio_measured_over_pred of 2.068 and 1.351 respectively -- composition is superlinear (measured damage exceeds the summed-table prediction by up to ~2x), not merely offset. WA4 is out-of-regime at 12/12 blocks (eps_eff up to 0.69 vs E1 boundaries 0.03/0.003), so this is consistent with compounding a Gaussian-regime-violating quantizer with a second distortion mechanism (merging). Resolution: WA4 removed from the precision menu everywhere (plan space, both solvers, both sequential stages); X8/X9 retained in E5_familyX.csv as evidence, never fit.
F_X1_wa4_menu_enforcement.wa4_exclusion_justification: WA4 excluded: out-of-regime at 12/12 blocks (eps_eff up to 0.69 vs boundaries 0.03/0.003) and empirically superlinear in composition (Family X ratios 1.35/2.07). WA6 retained under a documented exemption: violates the strict boundary at 6/12 blocks but composition is validated by E3 family-M (b=6, 0.93-1.27) and Family X (WA6-on-all-12 + merge, ratio 0.963).

F_X2_structured_subadditivity.title: Structured mild sub-additivity on the menu-consistent subset
F_X2_structured_subadditivity.statement: On the 10 menu-consistent configs, ratio_measured_over_pred correlates with n_quant_downstream_of_merge at r=-0.889 -- configs with MORE quantized blocks downstream of a merge point tend to measure BELOW their predicted damage (mild sub-additivity), not above. Mechanism: merging DELETES tokens whose quantization noise would otherwise have injected into the residual stream -- fewer surviving tokens carry quantization error forward, so downstream damage is structurally reduced. This sign is OPPOSITE to the QUOTA calibration-mismatch concern (which predicts downstream quantized blocks should measure ABOVE prediction, since their activation statistics have already been reshaped by an upstream merge relative to the clean-model calibration). The two mechanisms partially offset; the net effect measured here is mild sub-additivity, correctly captured within V1_E5's acceptance band.

F_collapse_staging_collapse.title: Staging collapse: JOINT ties (does not beat) BEST-SEQUENTIAL because the joint schedule is token-frontier-efficient
F_collapse_staging_collapse.statement: D_pred is separable in (schedule, bits) by construction (no cross term: DQ_TABLE entries don't depend on token count, DM_TABLE entries don't depend on bits), but the budget CONSTRAINT is coupled via N_l (a merge changes the token count, hence the BOPs cost, of every later block's bit choice). Conditional result: whenever the joint-optimal schedule is Pareto-efficient on the token axis ALONE (ignoring bits), a sufficiently strong staged search (both compression orders, a dense alpha grid, exact per-stage sub-solves) recovers it, because its stage-1 schedule selection is itself a token-axis Pareto search. Verified to hold at all 6 production budgets -- JOINT and BEST-SEQUENTIAL select bit-identical plans at every budget, which is why G1's measured delta_top1 is exactly 0.000pp with a zero-width CI: the necessary consequence of plan collapse, not a statistical artifact. Corollary: any joint>staged margin under the REAL (measured-cost) objective, rather than the predicted D_pred proxy, would have to come from cost-structure NON-additivity this predicted-cost model does not capture -- i.e. a case where the truly optimal schedule is NOT token-frontier-efficient, so no staged threshold search could reach it even in principle.

D4_amendment.statement: Design Decision D4 is amended to an operational 'validated composition territory' criterion: a precision menu entry is admissible only if its composition with the token axis has been empirically validated (E3 family-M and/or Family X measurements), not merely if it individually sits near the E1 linear regime boundary. WA8 and WA6 both satisfy this (WA6 under a documented exemption: violates the strict per-block regime boundary at 6/12 blocks, but E3 family-M (b=6, ratios 0.93-1.27) and Family X (WA6-on-all-12 + merge, ratio 0.963) empirically validate its composition behavior). WA4 does not satisfy this criterion (F-X1) and is excluded.

spec_error_note: The original E5 spec's precision menu {FP16,WA8,WA6,WA4} was itself a spec error: including WA4 violated Design Decision D4's (now-amended) validated-composition-territory requirement, since WA4 is out-of-regime at all 12 blocks and was never validated for quant+merge composition before being placed in the plan space. This is the second on-the-record spec correction this experiment (the first being gate (e)'s original 'recover every discrete Pareto-frontier point' criterion at STOP-1, corrected to the achievable convex-hull claim).
